title: Gibson Dove Authentication Guide
description: Identify a vintage Gibson Dove: compare model features, dating evidence, original parts, repairs and reissues, with photographs from Joe’s archive.
alt: 1976 Gibson Dove in Ebony with bird pickguard and split parallelogram inlays
caption: 1976 Gibson Dove in Ebony from my completed Reverb listing. The listing records a small crack between the bridge pins; this is a condition example, not the table’s excellent-original benchmark.

faqs.q: Can a serial number authenticate my Gibson Dove?
faqs.a: No. The number must agree with the body, neck, trim, hardware and construction. Some Gibson number sequences overlap, and an interior factory order number must be interpreted in context.

faqs.q: Does a repair mean the guitar is not authentic?
faqs.a: No. Model identity, manufacture date and originality are separate findings. A repaired instrument may be authentic, while its changed parts and condition still need disclosure.

faqs.q: Can a modern reissue look like a vintage example?
faqs.a: Yes. Period-style appointments are deliberately reproduced. Confirm the actual manufacturing date, serial system, construction and paperwork before using a vintage price comparison.
